To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the prevalence of chronic medical diseases among women of reproductive ages is increasing and that the Affordable Care Act provides an opportunity to improve the health care of women of reproductive ages.
the prevalence of chronic diseases and chronic disease risk behaviors are on the rise among women of reproductive and child bearing ages and that these conditions and risk behaviors can be prevented.
the health of women in their reproductive years affects their future health and the health of their offspring.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the health of women before, during, after pregnancy and beyond.
understanding how to prevent chronic diseases in women of reproductive aged women.
improving the health of women before, during, after pregnancy, and throughout their lives by reducing chronic diseases, chronic disease risk factors, and adverse pregnancy outcomes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
chronic diseases among reproductive aged women is a significant problem in the United States.
chronic disease prevention in reproductive aged women is a public health priority that requires a public health response that includes surveillance, health promotion and disease intervention.
the health of reproductive age women is a priority for the health of the United States.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we need more data to inform our programs, we need more research to inform our programs and we need more programs to inform our research.
the health of women in the reproductive age group is an important component of the overall health of the population and the health of future children.
women of reproductive age need to be healthy before pregnancy and during the childbearing years, and that we need to do more to ensure their health.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the health of women is not only important for the health of their families and communities but is also important for the health and future of our nation.
women's health is not just about pregnancy, but rather a life course approach to improving health.
the health of women in their reproductive years is critical to the health of future mothers and babies.
